title: A payload carrying both imp[] and seatbid[] is resolved as a request, not silently one or the other
specNotes: OpenRTB 2.6 §3.2.1 (BidRequest) and §4.2.1 (BidResponse) are mutually exclusive top-level shapes: a request carries `imp[]`, a response carries `seatbid[]`. Neither object is ever documented with both arrays at once, so a payload carrying both is malformed with respect to either object, not a legitimate third shape.

This corpus documents the tool's actual, spec-consistent resolution rule for that malformed case rather than treating it as unspecified: `imp[]` wins detection (it is checked first), the payload is validated as a BidRequest only, and `payload.ambiguous_both_sides` says explicitly which side was picked and that the other side was ignored, instead of silently validating one side with no acknowledgement that the input was ambiguous.

The stray `seatbid` key also trips the unknown-fields checker as an exact field name on the wrong object (`payload.field_wrong_object`, WARNING) — a second, independent, and equally correct signal that the payload mixes the two objects; `maxLevel: warning` tolerates it without hard-coding the exact count of secondary findings.

This is a documented correct-behavior case, not a defect: it exercises the `payload.ambiguous_both_sides` resolution path described in the core validation map (index.js's detectType-adjacent ambiguity handling).
